:::{#def-residual}
#### Residuals and squared errors

Let $\mX$ be an $n \times p$ matrix, $\vy \in \reals^n$, and $\vb \in \reals^p$.
The **residual vector** of $\vb$ is $\vec\eps(\vb) \eqdef \vy - \mX\vb$,
and its entries $\eps_i = y_i - (\mX\vb)_i$ are the **residuals**.
The square $\eps_i^2$ is the $i$th **squared error**, and their sum

$$
\vec\eps \cdot \vec\eps = \sum_{i=1}^n \eps_i^2 = \norm{\vy - \mX\vb}^2
$$

is the **residual sum of squares**.
A [least squares solution](linear-algebra.qmd#def-least-squares) of $\mX\vb = \vy$
makes $\norm{\vy - \mX\vb}$ as small as possible,
and so makes the residual sum of squares as small as possible too.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-residual}
#### Residuals of a constant fit

Let $\mX = \tp{(1, 1)}$ ($n = 2$, $p = 1$) and $\vy = \tp{(1, 3)}$.
For $\vb = (2)$, $\mX\vb = \tp{(2, 2)}$, so

$$
\ba
\vec\eps(\vb)
&= \tp{(1, 3)} - \tp{(2, 2)}
&& \text{(definition of the residual vector)}
\\
&= \tp{(-1, 1)},
&& \text{(subtract entry by entry)}
\ea
$$

the squared errors are $(-1)^2 = 1$ and $1^2 = 1$,
and the residual sum of squares is $1 + 1 = 2$.
For $\vb = (1)$ the residuals are $0$ and $2$,
and the residual sum of squares is $0 + 4 = 4$.

:::
